titleEn: The Gāyatrī asks the Sun to set our thoughts in motion.
sanskrit: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः । तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥
transliteration: oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ · tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi · dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt
meaningHi: ॐ — धरती, आकाश, स्वर्ग। उस सविता — सूर्य — के सबसे श्रेष्ठ तेज का हम ध्यान करते हैं। वह हमारी बुद्धि को सही राह पर चलाए।
meaningEn: Oṃ — earth, sky, heaven. We meditate on the finest radiance of Savitṛ, the Sun who impels all things. May he set our thoughts in motion.
sayItLike: Om bhoor bhuvah svaha · tat savitur varenyam · bhargo devasya dheemahi · dhiyo yo nah prachodayaat

words.grammar: bhūḥ becomes bhūr before the next vowel (sandhi)

words.glossEn: of Savitṛ — the Sun who impels
words.grammar: of Savitṛ — genitive; savituḥ becomes savitur before a vowel
bhargaḥ becomes bhargo before a voiced sound

words.glossEn: of the god — the shining one

words.grammar: we-may-meditate — first person plural, a wish
dhiyaḥ becomes dhiyo before a voiced sound

words.glossEn: may he set in motion — inspire

source.ref: 3.62.10 (Viśvāmitra); the oṃ + three vyāhṛtis prefix is Yajurvedic sandhyā liturgy (cf. Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 2.11)
source.note: Addressed to Savitṛ, the impelling sun; the goddess Gāyatrī as a person is later Purāṇic devotion. Taught here without Vedic accents (svara).

significance.textSays: A prayer to Savitṛ — the Sun as the one who impels — that his finest radiance set our thoughts moving.
significance.traditionSays: Recited at the three sandhyās — dawn, noon, dusk; the mantra given at the sacred-thread ceremony. Our stance: everyone may learn it, free.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That reciting it produces any outcome. It is a prayer for clear thought, quoted exactly.
